This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 15-04-2024, the petitioner was going towards Bengaluru city from her village Rayappanahalli, as a pillion rider, on a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ES-6444,
ridden by her brother Mahesh P., along with her relative Madhushree M., slowly,
cautiously, on the correct side of Shidlagatta-Bengaluru road.

On the way at about 8.40 a.m., infront of Primary School, Ramalingapura Village, Shidlagatta Taluk,
Chikkaballapura District, the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477 came from Shidlagatta side, with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came towards wrong side of the road and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, all the occupants of the motorcycle knocked down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Chikkaballapura, wherein she took first aid treatment and then she was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, she was working as an agriculturist and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Dibburahalli Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has contended that, the driver of his car bearing No.KA-40-A- 9477 was driving the same on the left side of Shidlaghatta road, slowly, carefully and cautiously, by observing all traffic rules and regulations, as there was no traffic on the said road.

When the said car reached at the alleged place of accident, the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES-6444, who was not wearing helmet, not holding valid driving licence, rode the same along with two pillion riders, at high speed, in a rash and negligent and due to high speed he lost control over his motorcycle and dashed against the car Nalina P vs Srikanth H N on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150706858/
2 bearing No.KA-40-A-9477 and fell down and sustained simple injuries.

Further it is contended that, he is the registered certificate owner of the car bearing No.KA-40-A- 9477 and all the records pertaining to the said car are standing in his name and the said car was insured with the respondent No.2 i.e. IFFCO-TOKIO General Insurance Co. Ltd., under the policy No.13522742 and same was valid from 12-06-2023 to 11-06-2024 and as on the alleged date of accident the insurance policy was valid and in force and the driver of his car was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said car.
If at all, the petitioner is entitled for any compensation, the same has to be paid or indemnified by the respondent No.2.
Further, he has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by her.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477 in favour of respondent No.1 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 56, 66, 147, 149(2) and 150 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non- compliance of provision under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9477 was not at all involved in the alleged accident, the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA- 03-ES-6444 was solely responsible for the alleged accident, the said car is falsely implicated by the petitioner in collusion with the owner of the vehicle, hospital authorities and police, to get compensation from this respondent.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident.
As such, he has violated Section 129 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, as per the police documents, three persons were traveling on a two-wheeler, in the event of three persons traveling on a motorcycle each one of them has contributed their negligence in causing the accident.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the car was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the particular class of vehicle as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.1 knowing fully well that the driver did not have valid driving licence as on the date of accident has entrusted his vehicle to the said driver.
The jurisdictional police after investigation filed charge-sheet against the insured vehicle driver under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C. and 181 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Thereby, the owner of the vehicle has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it is contended that, the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9477 was not holding valid fitness certificate and permit as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by her.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

Due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous on her right leg and left hand.

involvement
of car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477 in the said accident
, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident
, are not in dispute.

But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-ES-6444 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner in collusion with the police authorities and respondent No.1 has got registered a false case against the driver of said car, to get wrongful gain from the respondents.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

They have neither adduced any evidence, nor they have produced any document to show that, the said accident has solely taken place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ES-6444 himself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477 and dashing the same to the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ES-6444 of the petitioner, from opposite direction

. Though, the learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 have cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ES-6444 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
14. But, it is pertinent to note that, admittedly, at the time of accident the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES- 6444 was riding the same along with two pillion riders.

There are every chances that, due to three persons traveling on a motorcycle, which is meant for two persons, there would be congestion to the rider of said motorcycle and he might have lost control resulting in the accident.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Nalina P vs Srikanth H N on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150706858/

But, as there is no evidence on record to show that, the very act of three persons riding on the motorcycle has directly contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim, this Court is of the opinion that, holding the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES- 6444 liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10% would be justified and will meet the ends of justice.

15. Further, the Ex.P.9 spot mahazar and Ex.P.10 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on left side of Dibburahalli-Shidlagatta road, infront of Primary School,
Ramalingapura Village, Shidlagatta Taluk, Chikkaballapura, in between car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A- 9477 and oncoming motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES-6444 of the petitioner.
As per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477.

Further, the investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.11, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge- sheet has not been challenged by the owner-cum-driver of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

16. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.2 wound certificate, Ex.P.3 discharge summary,
Ex.P.4 OPD book, Ex.P.6 x-ray films (total 7), Ex.P.12 disability assessment chart, Ex.P.13 x-rays (total 2) and Ex.P.16 case- sheet it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
The petitioner has sustained fracture mid shaft of right femur and fracture distal end of left radius.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents No.1 and 2 to show that, the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents No.1 and 2 have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 15-04-2024 at about 8.40 a.m., on Dibburahalli-Shidlagatta road, in front of Primary School, Ramalingapura Village,
Shidlagatta Taluk, Chikkaballapura, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477.
But, the petitioner has failed to prove that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.

For the reasons stated supra this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-ES-6444 is also liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10% in the cause of accident.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-A-9477 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained fracture mid shaft of right femur and fracture distal end of left radius.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock,
loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.1.
As per Ex.P.1, the date of birth of the petitioner is 04-09-1999.
The accident has taken place on 15-04-2024 at about 8.40 a.m.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 25 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered fracture mid shaft of right femur and fracture distal end of left radius and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgeries.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 57.32% to right lower limb, 15.99% to left upper limb and 21% to the whole body.

Further, the Ex.P.2 wound certificate, Ex.P.3 discharge summary, Ex.P.4 OPD book,
Ex.P.6 x-ray films (total 7), Ex.P.12 disability assessment chart, Ex.P.13 x-rays (total 2) and Ex.P.16 case sheet clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and for the said injuries she has undergone surgery.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any Nalina P vs Srikanth H N on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150706858/
7 disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

If the disability had been assessed after future surgery,
perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further,
it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 15-04-2024 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 04-10- 2025, which is after lapse of one year and five months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the fractures are united, implants are in situ and the petitioner is of tender age.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained,
avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record,
this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was working as an agriculturist and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Further, she has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident she is unable to do her work.
The respondents have specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
She has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was working as an agriculturist and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2024.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,98,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 25 years is 18.

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,98,000 X 15/100 X 18 = Rs.5,34,600/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 8 medical bills, as per Ex.P.5.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.1,730/- towards medical expenses.

Therefore,
the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,730/- under the head of medical expenses.

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
fracture mid shaft of right femur and fracture distal end of left radius.
As per Ex.P.3 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 9 days from 15-04-2024 to 23-04- 2024, in Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.3 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 9 days in Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
She might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 9 = Rs.9,000/-
is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.3 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 9 days in Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
She might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 9 =
Rs.7,200/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Rayappanahalli Village, Sidlagatta Taluk,
Chikkaballapura District, the accident has taken place on Dibburahalli-Shidlagatta road, in front of Primary School, Ramalingapura Village, Shidlagatta Taluk, Chikkaballapura District and the petitioner has taken treatment at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 9 days as in-patient at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by her.
She might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost her income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.16,500 x 2 =
Rs.33,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 25 years and unfortunately she has suffered fracture mid shaft of right femur and fracture distal end of left radius.
Further, she has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 15% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants, which would cost Rs.30,000/-.

But,
admittedly the P.W.2 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

22. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A- 9477.
The insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 bearing No.13522742, in respect of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477, was valid from 12-06-2023 to 11-06- 2024.
As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-40-A-9477 the accident in question has taken place.
